odoo 19 breaking changes pitfalls checklist migration
Odoo 19 breaking-changes checklist (read before writing Python)

Every item below crashed a real install/run on Odoo 19 — do NOT write pre-17 idioms: 1. `_sql_constraints = [...]` is IGNORED -> `_x_uniq = models.Constraint('UNIQUE(a,b)', "msg")`. 2. `name_get()` removed -> override `_compute_display_name()`, read `.display_name`. 3. Search views: `<group expand="0" string="...">` is INVALID -> plain `<group>`. 4. `attrs=` / `states=` on view elements removed -> direct `invisible="..."` expressions. 5. List views use `<list>`, not `<tree>`. 6. BaseModel has `__slots__`: `self._anything = x` on a recordset raises AttributeError. 7. `odoo.__file__` can be None -> anchor paths on `odoo.modules.module.__file__`. 8. `@api.multi` / `@api.one` do not exist. 9. Controllers: `type='jsonrpc'` (not `type='json'`). 10. Never hand-write .po files; generate via base.language.export, then fill msgstr. 11. Chatter: model must inherit `mail.thread` and the form view include `<chatter/>` (Odoo 19 tag) to show messages/followers. 12. Smart buttons: use `type="object"` + a Python method returning the action. NEVER `type="action"` with `active_id`/`id` in the context — the view validator raises "Access Rights Inconsistency: field active_id does not exist" and the module fails to install. (This error is only visible with --log-handler odoo.tools.convert:DEBUG.) 13. A view referencing an action/record by xmlid must load AFTER that xmlid is defined — order the manifest data list accordingly (actions before the views/menus that reference them). 14. Two fields with the same `string=` label on one model log a warning; give related m2o/o2m fields distinct labels. 15. A model method that creates a log/history/audit record for a user who lacks create rights on that model must sudo() that create — else non-privileged users get AccessError. See odoo_docs "sudo". 16. A STORED computed field whose value comes from a search() on ANOTHER model cannot be tracked by @api.depends; recompute it from that other model's write/create/unlink. See odoo_docs "stored computed search". 17. OWL client action: `static props = {}` fails prop validation in debug mode — spread `standardActionServiceProps` (import from @web/webclient/actions/ action_service). The .xml t-name MUST equal the JS `static template` string. 18. Frontend DATA CONTRACT: a backend data method must return EVERY field the UI reads — including any field you filter/group/sort by client-side. If the UI filters a list by category, each row in the returned data must carry category. (Sandbox install does NOT run JS — verify dashboards/widgets by rendering.) 19. Dashboard/report method reading MANY records: sudo() the read-only aggregation (record rules + ACLs otherwise raise AccessError for most users and the OWL dashboard crashes at onWillStart), AND gate the menu to the data's group. See odoo_docs "dashboard". 20. Odoo 19: res.users groups field is `group_ids` (was `groups_id`). Manager groups usually imply the user group via implied_ids; a record rule on the user group also constrains managers unless a broader manager rule/sudo is used.

verified: action_add_points create() without sudo -> AccessError for non-manager users who lack perm_create on the log model

# A method that writes an audit/log/points record on behalf of a user who does # NOT have create rights on that log model MUST use .sudo() for the create, # otherwise every non-privileged user hits AccessError. def action_add_points(self, points, reason=None): self.ensure_one() # sudo(): a normal user awards points but has no create right on the log self.env['loyalty.history'].sudo().create({ 'partner_id': self.id, 'points': points, 'reason': reason, }) self.loyalty_points += points # Rule of thumb: if a method's create()/write() targets a model whose access csv # does NOT grant the acting group that permission, sudo() that ORM call (and only # that call). Do not sudo() the whole method. Common for: activity/mail logs, # audit trails, history lines, sequence bumps, counters.

Dashboard/report data method: sudo() the aggregation + gate the menu

verified: get_dashboard_data without sudo -> AccessError for users outside the model's group / limited by a record rule; the OWL dashboard then crashes at onWillStart. Only caught by RENDERING (install does not call the method).

# A dashboard/report method aggregates across MANY records for reporting. Record # rules (e.g. "see only your own") and per-group ACLs will make plain reads raise # AccessError for most users -> the OWL component's onWillStart throws -> blank # dashboard. For a READ-ONLY org-wide aggregation, sudo() the reads: @api.model def get_dashboard_data(self): projects = self.env['pulse.project'].sudo().search([]) # sudo: read-only report tasks = self.env['pulse.task'].sudo().search([]) # ... aggregate, then return only the fields the UI needs ... return {'kpis': [...], 'recent': [ {'id': t.id, 'name': t.name, 'state': t.state, 'priority': t.priority} for t in tasks[:20]]} # include EVERY field the UI filters/shows
# AND gate the menu/action so only authorized users open the dashboard at all: # <menuitem id="menu_x_root" ... groups="module.group_x_user"/> # Rule of thumb: a menu whose action reads records restricted by ACL/record-rule # must be restricted to the same group, and org-wide report methods sudo() reads. # NOTE: install-testing does NOT run JS or call the method — verify a dashboard by # actually rendering it (the AccessError only appears at runtime).
